review.name: Warmun
review.case_for: Rule 1: named twice by Wikivoyage (Kimberley region page and Kununurra 'Go next') as the Purnululu entry point with a long-standing Aboriginal art scene; the Warmun Art Centre is a recognised gallery.
review.objection: Only one-line mentions, no own guide section, and an Aboriginal community where the visitor draw is the art centre rather than the town: the Warmun Art Centre may be the right spot, or it is a gateway village whose draw is the journey beyond (Pipiriki benchmark -> review).
review.would_go: standalone (or the Warmun Art Centre as the spot), about 160 km from the Purnululu centre

review.name: Lombadina
review.case_for: Re-looked for a counted source: Lombadina's own site invites visitors (day pass $10 per vehicle; craft shop, bush-timber church and beach open weekdays 8am-4pm; mud-crabbing, kayak and whale-watching tours), and a Lonely Planet Dampier Peninsula article (search snippet; the URL now redirects) names its Aboriginal-led tours. Visit Broome names it as one of the four peninsula communities.
review.objection: Only one counted source and that one not readable now; the community's own site is an operator page; a visit is on community terms with seasonal weekend closures, and the beach and church are modest.
review.would_go: standalone; with Cape Leveque and One Arm Point approved, a Dampier Peninsula destination becomes possible

review.name: Kalumburu
review.case_for: Wikivoyage Gibb River Road names it as the end of the 208 km Kalumburu Road, and Visit Broome's Gibb River Road page gives it a section (two counted sources); a remote mission community with beaches and fishing (Honeymoon Bay, McGowans Island).
review.objection: Neither source names something to see in the community itself, only the two permits needed to enter; access is at the Traditional Owners' discretion and may be closed. The candidate note is wrong: Mitchell Falls is reached from a turn-off on Kalumburu Road, not from Kalumburu.

review.name: Cape Leveque
review.case_for: Headland at the tip of the Dampier Peninsula, named by Wikivoyage Broome (Go next) and Lonely Planet (POI 'Cape Leveque (Kooljaman)'); a well-known Kimberley beach and red-cliff destination (rule 1).
review.objection: Kooljaman, the resort that held the visitor access, closed indefinitely on 1 Nov 2021 and no reopening was found; an operator says Cape Leveque point is closed indefinitely and access is limited (rule 2: open to the public is unconfirmed).
review.would_go: standalone; one of the three that would make a Dampier Peninsula destination

review.name: Buccaneer Archipelago
review.case_for: Island group named by Visit Broome (Derby: 'the islands of the Buccaneer Archipelago') and Wikivoyage Broome (boat trips reach it), and inside DBCA's Lalang-gaddam Marine Park; it is the place the Derby and Broome cruises go to.
review.objection: Visitors go for Horizontal Falls, a candidate of its own inside the archipelago; the archipelago as a whole is an area seen only from boats and planes, so it risks being a near-duplicate wrapper of Horizontal Falls.
review.would_go: fold into Horizontal Falls (skeptic: keep Horizontal Falls as the one spot)

review.name: Canning Stock Route
review.case_for: A 1,850 km historic 4WD route that Australia's North West's Halls Creek page names among the outback drives from Halls Creek and that Wikivoyage Kimberley mentions as a 'full-on expedition' (rule 1 met once).
review.objection: A route, not a place you stop at for half an hour; Wikivoyage calls it beyond its scope; most of its length and its southern trailhead (Wiluna) lie outside the Kimberley (probably wa-golden-outback / Pilbara), so the proposer must decide one region and pin it at the midpoint; permits needed.
review.would_go: not placed here: wa-golden-outback keeps it and places it once (run-wide decision)

review.objection: One passing sentence and nothing to do beyond a quiet beach; close to Gantheaume Point, so it may be a near-duplicate of that stop.

review.name: Kabbarli Lookout

review.objection: One source, which also calls the approach grubby through the port industrial area; a short look, similar red rocks to Gantheaume Point nearby.

review.objection: It is Willie Creek's pearl showroom: a shop with an attached tour (brief: shops and operators are rejected); one counted source.

review.objection: One sentence in one source, a dusk-only spectacle with no defined site, and a short look; may be too minor.

review.objection: Opens only weekday mornings Feb-Nov, by donation, a small single-room exhibit; one source.

review.objection: One sentence in one source; a ten-minute look; probably only worth it alongside the Boab Prison Tree.

review.would_go: answered by the proposed gibb-river-road destination if approved; otherwise a standalone spot at the route midpoint

review.objection: No distance, trail or managing agency named; possibly a local walk only. Needs a second source before it goes in.

review.name: Gwion Gwion Rock Paintings
review.case_for: Rule 1: Wikivoyage's Kimberley page features them (image and art context); internationally known rock art with high page views.
review.objection: Not one place: an art style found at hundreds of remote sites, mostly reached on guided tours or flights (an operator), and the candidate has no coordinates; better listed as a named accessible site (e.g. on the Mitchell Falls walk or near Kalumburu) if a source names one, otherwise mentioned in a destination description.
review.would_go: not one place: mention in descriptions, or a named accessible site if a source gives one

review.name: Chinatown
review.case_for: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Broome (fetched) names Chinatown as the traditional retail strip along Carnarvon St; Broome's historic pearling-era quarter is a stop most visitors walk.
review.objection: Rule 2: Wikivoyage describes it as mainly shops and cafes ('don't expect gongs'); without a second source naming something to see (heritage buildings, Sun Pictures, pearl showrooms) it is a shopping strip. Name 'Chinatown' needs a wiki disambiguator.
review.would_go: broome spot (wiki needs a disambiguator; Sun Pictures sits in it)

review.name: One Arm Point
review.case_for: Rule 1 re-look: Lonely Planet attraction 'Ardyaloon (One Arm Point)' and Visit Broome listing for the Ardyaloon Trochus Hatchery (fetched) name it as a Dampier Peninsula stop with hatchery tours and beaches.
review.objection: Several operators report the hatchery closed for repairs after cyclone damage; a community permit is needed; without the hatchery the draw is the views and crafts only.
review.would_go: standalone; one of the three for a Dampier Peninsula destination

review.name: Mount Elizabeth Station
review.case_for: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Gibb River Road (fetched) and Australia's North West Gibb River Road page ('Mt Elizabeth Station Stay') name it; the base for Wunnamurra and Warla gorges.
review.objection: Brief: accommodation and stations are rejected as businesses; the gorges are the places and should be the spots if sources name them. Keep only if the station itself is treated as a destination base.

review.name: Home Valley Station
review.case_for: Rule 1 re-look: Tourism Australia's Gibb River Road itinerary (fetched) uses Balanggarra Home Valley Station as a multi-night base 'where towering gorges meet waterfalls and billabongs', and Australia's North West lists it among the Gibb's main stops.
review.objection: It is a station resort (accommodation business); the gorges and Cockburn Range views it offers are the places, and none is named here as a spot.

review.name: Chamberlain Gorge
review.case_for: Rule 1: Tourism WA attraction page (fetched) names Chamberlain Gorge in El Questro Wilderness Park; the gorge is the place the cruise goes to.
review.objection: Rule 3 and 2: inside El Questro Wilderness Park and seen only on the operator's boat cruise (May-Sep), so it may be part of an El Questro spot rather than distinct.
review.would_go: standalone; with El Questro Gorge, makes El Questro Wilderness Park a destination (4 spots)

review.name: El Questro Gorge
review.case_for: Rule 1 re-look: El Questro's own walking-trail guide (elquestro.com.au, the park's operator; fetched) describes the El Questro Gorge Trail to Halfway Pool and Micking Pool; travel press (Australian Geographic) names it a highlight.
review.objection: Rule 3: part of El Questro Wilderness Park; no Wikivoyage or Tourism WA listing found, and the operator's own document is the only counted source; Emma Gorge is the park's better-known gorge.

not_destinations.why: two kept places; Tourism WA names it as a destination, so it becomes one if the owner approves Cape Leveque, Lombadina and One Arm Point (review).
two spots inside the park plus the park; with El Questro Gorge and Chamberlain Gorge approved from review it reaches four (Tourism WA names El Questro Wilderness Park).
two kept places (Yarliyil Art Gallery in review); Wolfe Creek Crater is about 106 km south.
one spot inside the park: a park needs four (or flagship status).
two places 100 km apart, seen from tours; Kimberley Marine Park was rejected as an administrative zone.
